rationale: Testing the scope statement just recorded about which entry points the disarmed proposal gate covers. The successor harness adds a read-index control in the same Node-API cluster: after node 3 is removed and re-added so its gate is disarmed, it issues a read-index request and then a proposal. If the gate covers only MsgProp traffic, the read-index request should complete with a read state while the proposal stays held and uncommitted.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process, with Ready handling, message delivery and conf-change application as in the other tests. Node 1 is elected in configuration {1,2,3}; a remove-3 ConfChange is proposed and applied on every node; an add-3 ConfChange re-admits node 3 with leader 1 unchanged. Then node 3 calls ReadIndex with a request context, the harness waits for the corresponding read state to appear in node 3's Ready stream, and afterwards node 3 calls Propose with a bounded context. Events record the read state's presence and index, the proposal's return behaviour and whether its payload was committed.
assumptions: Read-index completion is observed through Ready.ReadStates, which is the documented endpoint of a read-index request for the application.
Reliable, per-sender ordered in-process delivery and no ticks, so leader 1 stays in place.
The read state is matched by the request context sent by the harness, which is independent of the measured values.
excluded: ReadOnlyLeaseBased and read-index requests issued while the member is removed or leaderless
Message loss, ticks and configuration changes other than the removal and re-addition

experiment.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3}. Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose a remove-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's configuration excludes it, then propose an add-3 ConfChange and wait until node 3 is a voter again with leader still 1, which leaves node 3's proposal gate disarmed. Issue ReadIndex on node 3 with a fixed request context and wait until a read state carrying that context appears in node 3's Ready stream. Then invoke Node.Propose on node 3 with a 900 ms context, observe for 800 ms, and record the result and whether the payload is committed anywhere.
experiment.responsibility: Client-facing obligation boundary: a member whose proposals are held must still be able to obtain read-index completions, so the defect is confined to the MsgProp entry points rather than to the member's participation in general.

comparisons.description: A read state for the request context reached node 3's Ready stream while its proposal gate was disarmed.
The same member's proposal did not return inside the window.
That proposal's payload was not committed anywhere.

experiment.revision_reason: Harness and comparison change: a read-index control test was added to the same harness file, driving the same three-node Node-API cluster through remove-3 and add-3 so node 3's proposal gate is disarmed, then calling Node.ReadIndex on node 3 and waiting for a read state with the request context to appear in a Ready before invoking Node.Propose on the same node with a 900 ms context and an 800 ms window. Three comparisons cover the read state's arrival, the proposal not returning, and the proposal's payload not being committed. The read-index test is additive; the witness, flags, restart, joint-control and exploration tests in the file are unchanged.
